classification.difficultyReason: Identify the relevant transversal within rotated and composite figures, then compare the marked angles' interior positions and sides to classify each pair.

content.prompt: In each diagram, identify each pair of angles marked with $\alpha$ and $\beta$ as corresponding angles, alternating angles or co-interior angles.

spec.description: Two gently rising lines crossed by a steep rising transversal; both labels occupy corresponding upper-right sectors. Source decorative blue becomes black.
spec.mathematics: Corresponding positions; no parallel marks or angle arcs.
spec.answerVisibility: Labels and geometry are permanent givens; classification is hidden.

answer.worked: The angles occupy the same relative position at the two intersections, so they are corresponding angles.

spec.description: Two descending lines crossed by a gently rising transversal. Alpha is interior below the transversal at the left intersection; beta is interior above it at the right intersection.
spec.mathematics: Interior angles on opposite sides of the transversal.
spec.answerVisibility: Classification hidden; all source labels visible.

answer.worked: The angles lie between the two descending lines and on opposite sides of the transversal, so they are alternate angles.

spec.description: Horizontal lines crossed by a rising transversal; both labels are interior and right of the transversal.

answer.worked: Both angles are between the horizontal lines and on the same side of the transversal, so they are co-interior angles.

spec.description: Two steep descending lines crossed by a shallower descending transversal; labels are interior and on opposite sides of the transversal.

answer.worked: The angles lie between the steep lines and on opposite sides of the transversal, so they are alternate angles.

spec.description: Two steep rising lines crossed by a shallow rising transversal; labels lie between the steep lines below the transversal.

answer.worked: Both angles lie between the steep lines and below the transversal, so they are co-interior angles.

spec.description: Two descending lines crossed by a shallow rising transversal; both labels occupy the upper sector at their intersections.

answer.worked: The angles occupy matching positions above the transversal at the two intersections, so they are corresponding angles.

spec.description: Unmarked parallelogram; upper-left and lower-left interior angles labelled.
spec.mathematics: Top and bottom edges are crossed by the left side; marked angles are co-interior.

answer.worked: Using the left side as the transversal of the top and bottom edges, both marked angles are interior and on the same side of that transversal.

spec.description: Parallelogram with diagonal from lower-left to upper-right; labels between the diagonal and the horizontal edges.
spec.mathematics: Alternate positions with the diagonal as transversal.

answer.worked: The diagonal crosses the top and bottom edges. The marked angles lie between those edges on opposite sides of the diagonal, so they are alternate angles.

spec.description: Triangle with horizontal interior segment. Labels lie above each horizontal and left of the right side.
spec.mathematics: Corresponding positions using the right side as transversal.

answer.worked: Using the right side as the transversal, the angles occupy the same relative position above the two horizontal segments.

spec.description: Triangle with horizontal interior segment; labels between the horizontals and right of the left side.
spec.mathematics: Co-interior positions using the left side as transversal.

answer.worked: The left side crosses the two horizontal segments. Both marked angles lie between the segments on the same side of the left side.

spec.description: Inclined E with all three horizontal segments; labels above the lower and middle segments and right of the slope.

answer.worked: The sloping line crosses the lower and middle horizontal segments. Both angles occupy the position above the horizontal segment and to the right of the slope.

spec.description: Triangle between extended horizontal lines; alpha below the upper line and left of the left slope, beta above the lower line and right of that slope.
spec.mathematics: Alternate positions using the left slope as transversal.

answer.worked: The left sloping side crosses the two horizontal lines. The marked angles lie between the lines on opposite sides of that transversal.
